answer: To register, an agent locks tokens and sends a costly violet challenge marker that peers verify, so fake identities must burn real capital per account. Sybil resistance comes from staking a scarce, slashable bond tied to each identity. Good behavior returns the bond plus a reputation signal; misconduct slashes it and sends a negative ripple through the trust graph, warning others. Because cloning identities multiplies attacker cost linearly while honest agents pay once, mass sybil creation becomes economically irrational. This model fits agent once0004's threat model.
